title: Farfalle al Salmone
subtitle: Farfalle with smoked salmon, cream, and dill
excerpt: Farfalle al salmone is a quick pasta of smoked salmon stirred through a cream and dill sauce. It is light enough for a weeknight and good enough for a relaxed dinner with friends. The salmon goes in off the heat so it stays silky rather than cooking to a dry, grainy texture.
sourceNotes: Pasta with smoked salmon and cream became a popular Italian restaurant dish in the 1980s, reflecting the influence of Nordic smoked salmon as a luxury ingredient in Italian cooking during that period. The farfalle shape is traditionally associated with this sauce in Italian home cooking.

content.text: Farfalle al salmone is a cream-based pasta with smoked salmon that comes together in 15 minutes. The smoked salmon must go in off the heat: it only needs warming through, not cooking, and direct heat makes it grainy and overpowering. The sauce is cream, a splash of white wine, and dill; lemon zest added at the end lifts the richness.

items.prepNote: zest and a squeeze of juice

content.text: Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the shallots for 3 to 4 minutes until soft and translucent. Add the white wine and simmer for 2 minutes until reduced by half.
Pour in the double cream. Simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until the cream has reduced and coats the back of a spoon. Season lightly: smoked salmon adds its own salt.
Cook the farfalle in well-salted boiling water until 1 minute short of al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain.

Take the cream sauce off the heat. Add the farfalle and a splash of pasta water, tossing to coat. Add the smoked salmon, dill, lemon zest, and a small squeeze of lemon juice. Toss gently: the salmon will warm through in the heat of the pasta. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Smoked salmon is dry and grainy in the finished dish
items.cause: Salmon was added while the pan was still on the heat
items.fix: The pan must be off the heat when the salmon goes in. It will warm through in 30 to 60 seconds from the residual heat of the pasta and sauce.

items.cause: Smoked salmon and salted pasta water together are often enough salt without any extra
items.fix: Season the cream sauce very lightly before adding the salmon, then taste once the salmon is in before adjusting. Lemon juice can balance saltiness without adding more sodium.

items.cause: Cream was boiled too hard or reduced too far
items.fix: Simmer rather than boil the cream sauce. Add pasta water at the tossing stage to loosen and help emulsify.

content.text: Pasta al salmone became a fixture of Italian restaurant menus in the 1980s, when smoked salmon became a prestige ingredient across Europe. The cream and dill combination was drawn from Scandinavian flavours and became a standard dish in trattorias. Farfalle is the usual pasta for it. The butterfly wings hold the cream sauce well.
